First public release of pb, a small tool that turns one `build.toml` into a `.deb`, an `.rpm`, an AppImage and an AUR `PKGBUILD`. It writes every format itself, so you don't need `dpkg-deb`, `rpmbuild`, `appimagetool` or `mksquashfs` on the machine. pb is a single static binary for x86_64 and aarch64.

## What it does

- **Builds your project.** CMake, Cargo, Go and plain Makefile projects are detected and built in release mode. Anything else, like scripts or prebuilt binaries, goes in with `--binary`.
- **Packs it four ways at once.** All formats are built in parallel and land in `~/pb-builds/`, or in one folder with `--out`.
- **Gets the details right.** The architecture comes from the ELF header, scripts become `all`/`noarch`/`any`, and pb warns when a binary needs a newer glibc than older distros ship.
- **Makes Go binaries portable.** Go is built without cgo, so the binary is static and runs anywhere. If a project really needs cgo, pb falls back and tells you.
- **Writes an AUR package.** You get a `PKGBUILD` and `.SRCINFO`: a `-git` package for git repos, otherwise a source tarball with a real checksum.
- **Supports desktop apps when you ask.** With `gui = true` it adds a `.desktop` entry and an icon. CLI tools ship just the binary.

## Commands

- `pb build [DIR]` builds packages.
- `pb debug [DIR]` reports on your system, installed tools and how pb sees the project.
- `pb debug FILE` looks inside a `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` or binary and tells you if it will run here.
- `pb update` moves to the newest version tag after checking its sha256.
- `pb install`, `pb uninstall`, `pb repair`, `pb clear cache` and `pb lang ru|en` cover the rest.

## Install

```sh
curl -fLo pb https://github.com/Qwarwin4/pb/releases/download/v0.1/pb-0.1-$(uname -m)
chmod +x pb && sudo ./pb install
```

Or grab the `.deb`, `.rpm`, AppImage or `PKGBUILD` below. `sha256sums.txt` has the checksums.

Tested on Debian 12, Ubuntu 20.04 and 24.04, Fedora, Rocky 8, openSUSE Leap, Alpine and Arch.
